figures.note: Investigated products that were changed, rewritten or sent back.

figures.note: The answer stood; the figure did not.

savings.label: Representative time saved
savings.note: Against how long the same work is assumed to take unaided.

savings.label: Estimated AI investigation cost
savings.note: Estimated model and image-processing cost only; excludes claim payouts and representative labor.

savings.label: Left over
savings.note: The valued time, less what the investigating cost.

assumptions.label: A representative's hour
assumptions.description: What an hour of a support representative's time is taken to cost, including employment costs. Every dollar saving on this screen is hours multiplied by this rate. PROVISIONAL — the figure is ours, not ShipBob's.

assumptions.label: Investigating one product
assumptions.description: What it is taken to cost to investigate one claim, counting the AI and the images it looks at. It is subtracted from the saving, so the figure shown is what is left after paying for the system. A claim the quick checks stopped costs nothing and is charged nothing. PROVISIONAL — the figure is ours, not ShipBob's.

assumptions.label: One product, done unaided
assumptions.description: How long one damaged product would take a representative to work through from scratch, with no report to start from. Time saved is this less the time they actually spent reviewing. PROVISIONAL — nobody has timed the old way of working.

assumptions.label: One stopped claim, done unaided
assumptions.description: How long a claim that cannot be processed would take a representative to establish and close by hand. Much less than an investigation, because the four checks are quick questions with clear answers. PROVISIONAL — nobody has timed it.

data.title: Taken exactly as recommended, week by week
data.summary: Across the period, 67% of investigated products and 79% of stopped claims went out untouched.

data.title: How much a representative changed
data.summary: Across the period 67% went out untouched, 14% had only their wording changed, 11% had an amount or an outcome changed, and 8% were sent back.

data.title: How sure the system said it was, against how often it was accepted
data.summary: Each bar is how often a representative accepted the advice. The band behind it is how sure the system said it was. A bar shorter than its band means the system was more confident than it turned out to deserve.

data.summary: Each bar is how often that kind of claim went out exactly as the system produced it, and the groups are ordered by how far apart their bars are. A group near the top sorts the work before anybody starts on it; one near the bottom says that way of sorting claims does not help.

data.title: How often each recommendation was changed
data.summary: A bar is the share of that recommendation a representative did not accept as it stood. A recommendation nobody made has no bar.

data.title: How long a review took, week by week
data.summary: The average review took 8 min across the period.

data.title: Candidate rules, scored
data.caveat: A candidate rule is only worth discussing if representatives agreed with the system at least 95% of the time across at least 200 decisions. Both numbers are ours and neither has been agreed with anyone. Meeting the bar is not permission: FR-2.9 says a person approving is the only way a claim can be released, and no figure on this screen changes that. PROVISIONAL.
